source_ref: Geiger et al. (2025) Psychological Science doi:10.1177/09567976251335585. Wording: osf.io/6hny4 (Materials, Study 1; CC BY 4.0) surveys.zip -> Climate_Change_Beliefs_Canada.qsf (the administered Qualtrics survey; English base text). Code<->column crosswalk: osf.io/wcgja preparation_S1.Rmd rename() block, and osf.io/r2byz Codebook.pdf Table 1/Table 3. Raw data: osf.io/r2byz data_raw.zip (CC BY 4.0).
note:
Item codes are the cleaned data.rds column names (IRW script pivots them unchanged); the authors' preparation_S1.Rmd renames each from a raw Qualtrics export column (own.ccb=OwnCCBeliefs, other.ccb.main..know=OtherCCBeliefs_1..5, exp.change.low/high=Expectation_Changes_1/2, exp.support.low/high=Expectation_Support_1/2, discuss/own.change/own.support/efficacy=Discuss/Changes/Support/Efficacy), and the codebook prints the same code->wording table. Wording is the Canada .qsf English base text, not the codebook (the codebook paraphrases slightly: 'not at all responsible' vs administered 'not responsible at all'; 'do not know' vs 'does not know'; lowercase option labels). Deviations: HTML/bold stripped and whitespace collapsed; piped fields ${e://Field/Nationality_plural_en} and ${e://Field/Country_en} replaced by the codebook's own placeholders [citizens] and [country]; an invisible white-text 'xxxxxxx' spacer in the other.ccb.trend choice removed; discuss/efficacy endpoint labels shipped without their leading scale numeral ('1
Not at all willing' -> 'Not at all willing'), points 2-6 blank (they display bare numerals). Resp coding: own.ccb is stored 0-4 because preparation_S1.Rmd does own.ccb - 1 on the QSF recodes 1-5 (codebook Table 1 still says 1-5; the data and script say 0-4). efficacy: QSF 99 'I don't know' -> NA by the authors, 999 'I don't believe in (human-caused) climate change' -> NA by the IRW script; neither option is shipped since neither code is in the live table (247 NA resp rows remain in the live table). Slider items (0-100, OtherCCBeliefs sum-to-100, Expectation_* two-slider pairs) ship one row per live level with option_text blank; the shared question text is section_prompt per slider block. Language: 12 administered languages across 11 countries (UserLanguage in raw files: PT-BR 723, EN 439+2, FR-CA 41, ZH-S 835, DE 580, HI 1330, ID 959, IT 518, JA 737, ES 974, PL 548, TH 465, raw rows); base fields hold the English (Canada) administration, which is verbatim for EN respondents; every other language's wording is recoverable from the same surveys.zip (.qsf Language blocks) but the schema holds one text per item. English base text in the other 10 .qsf files adds a 'For the following question, please consider what [citizens] think about climate change.' preface to discuss/own.change/own.support that neither the Canada English nor any translation carries; Canada English followed. Rights: the items are the study's own survey (own.ccb is YouGov Globalism-style wording); deposit CC BY 4.0 (OSF API licence on 6hny4 and r2byz); no rights holder restriction located or quotable, so silence = permission. Mapping verified row-by-row (verify_climatechange_geiger_2025.R).
public_note: Respondents in Brazil, China, Germany, India, Indonesia, Italy, Japan, Mexico, Poland, Thailand and French-speaking Canada answered translated versions; the item text shown is the English (Canada) administration, with [citizens] and [country] standing for the nationality and country name piped in per country, and every translation is in the study's Qualtrics files at osf.io/6hny4.
